label: thm-second-derivative-test
tail:
VERDICT: CLEAN
BOUNDARY: The hypothesis “f'' exists and is continuous near c” forces the domain of f to contain an open interval around c (otherwise f'' could not exist at points arbitrarily close to c). Hence all interval-dependent theorems are applicable. The sign‑preservation step (from continuity of f'' at c) follows directly from the ε‑δ definition; no counterexample falsifies the claim under the given hypotheses. Degenerate cases (isolated point, empty domain, etc.) are excluded by the existence of f''(c).
SOURCES: All four supplied dependencies were inspected: `def-continuity-real` (provides the definition that yields the sign‑preservation fact), `thm-monotonicity-from-the-derivative` (gives the strict monotonicity from the sign of the derivative, used for f' and f), `def-derivative` (defines the derivative and its domain restrictions), and `def-higher-derivatives-and-smoothness` (defines f''). Each supports the necessary inferences without mismatch.
CHECKED: The title, the public statement, every numbered proof step (1.1, 1.2, 2.1, 3.1), and the Remarks were examined. No fatal defect was found; any minor omissions (e.g., the explicit ε‑δ derivation of the sign‑preservation neighbourhood) are quickly closable and within the explicitly acceptable tolerances.
